title: Oil paint strokes carry and smear colour and show bristle ridges
goal: The oil paint brush behaves like a loaded bristle brush: it lays down thick colour that runs out along a stroke, picks up and smears the paint already on the canvas, and leaves bristle ridges that catch the light. How loaded the brush is and how much it smears are its own settings.
notes:
Umbrella: a-brush-tool-paints-with-realistic-charcoal-chal (the user's ask, 2026-10-24). Design: docs/design/brushes.md, read it first; its decisions are settled unless this task's runner finds one cannot work, in which case they say so in the log and in the doc.

Design doc decision 4: bristle-and-pickup in the spirit of IMPaSTo (Baxter et al. 2004): a per-bristle colour reservoir picking up from the layer, a height channel lit at render. Likely a Metal or Core Image kernel.
acceptance: A stroke shows bristle streaks along its direction and lit ridges, not a flat fill
Painting across an earlier stroke drags its colour along and mixes it; Smear sets how much
Load sets how far a stroke goes before the brush runs dry
Measured bars the round tip fails: colour carried past the crossing point when one stroke crosses another, and ridge contrast inside a stroke
A walk with no flags paints two crossing strokes by pointer drag, with real window pictures in the audit

log.note: deps set by the umbrella's planning run: pressing-b-picks-a-brush-that-paints-freehand-st

Adversarial review before building: a Photoshop/Procreate painter expects the oil brush to blend with what is on the layer and to run out; the app has no colour reservoir or height channel, so built both in the marking half. Pickup can only read the paint layer the stroke lands on (renderer replays a layer alone; non-destructive rule), so a stroke over a screenshot never smears the screenshot. Load/Smear have no controls yet: that is the settings slice (each-brush-shows-its-own-settings-in-the-tool-op), not a gap in this one.

Chose a flat brush footprint (square ends, bell along the stroke) over a round filbert because the round one left visible dab arcs and uneven cover at the edges; chose easing the heading at 0.15 per step because the real window showed scallops from the hand's wobble at 0.6. Chose a TaskLocal PaintRasterizer.plainRound for the round-tip yardstick over keeping .oil as the baseline, since oil now has its own marking.

Looked at: oil-sheet (defaults, Smear 0/40/100, Load 20/70/100, mixing, round tip), oil-close at 4x, and the walk's 4-smeared-sc crop. They show opaque streaked strokes with lit ridges, red/black carried past the crossing fading back, dry-brush ends; the round tip row is flat and carries nothing. Left rough: 12 MP paint layer bakes at ~1.15 px/pt, so zoomed past ~140% the stroke softens on release (walk failed at 172% with 1.3%); folded into painting-keeps-up-with-the-pointer-on-a-12-megap with an acceptance item. Other rough lines stay in the audit only.

Oil Paint is a flat bristle brush (Sources/PhotonzRender/OilPaint.swift): streaks with lit ridges (ridge contrast 0.041, bar 0.025, plain round 0.001); picks up and carries colour past a crossing, mixing, set by Smear (0.33 at default, bar 0.10; Smear 0 0.015, 100 0.65; round 0.001); runs dry by Load (6/15/21 brush widths at 20/70/100). OilRenderingTests incl. live-equals-landed; full suite green (14527). Walk oil-paint-smears-and-ridges-walk, no flags, two crossing pointer drags, real window captures in queue/audits/2026-10-25-oil-paint.json; 0.6-0.7 ms median per move, held vs landed 0.14%/0.42%.
